statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low at 12% while stress is elevated at 57%, reflecting a fourth consecutive Nasdaq-100 lower close driven by long-end Treasury yields and an energy risk premium, set against an overnight futures band that has stayed contained and two-sided.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD across the full 24-hour horizon. Conditional risk is concentrated in two scheduled structural checkpoints: the 13:30 UTC cash open together with the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, published as the narrow 13:00-14:00 UTC danger window, and the 19:00-20:00 UTC monthly options-expiration settlement into the cash close. Both map to EA_ON in the forecast rather than to a block. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Contained overnight band keeps Nasdaq-100 mean reversion intact after a fourth lower close, with expiration Friday and a flash PMI as the day's checkpoints
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,213.17 on 20 August, down 0.72% and roughly 2.5% on the week, a fourth consecutive lower close that leaves the index on pace to end a three-week advance. The decline has been a grind rather than a rout: the 20 August session traded between 29,378.81 and 29,118.07 and closed about 95 points above its low, so retracements have remained available throughout the drawdown. Overnight, NQ futures traded 29,363.25, up 0.21%, inside a contained 124-point band of 29,274.25 to 29,398.50 and above the prior cash close, with two-way movement and no observed one-way structure. The driver of the weekly decline remains the long end of the Treasury curve. The 30-year yield is 5.251% and the 10-year 4.701%, both essentially unchanged overnight after Thursday reversed the relief that followed the Treasury's announcement that it would double long-bond buybacks to $4 billion per operation. Official H.15 data through 19 August put the 2-year at 4.19%, the 10-year at 4.65% and the 30-year at 5.19%. Volatility is elevated but not disorderly: the VIX closed at 16.01 after a 7.5% daily rise, and delayed cross-asset context shows VIX futures easing, gold firmer and WTI slightly lower near $86.37 after a roughly 6% weekly gain tied to the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption. Cross-sectional tone is conflicting rather than aligned: megacaps were broadly lower in the prior session with seven of eight names down, while the semiconductor complex was mixed to positive. Under the risk definitions that conflict raises stress and lowers directional conviction, it does not by itself establish a tail path. The scheduled day is light, with the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC the only notable release, but 21 August is the August monthly options expiration and CME equity index futures halt for the week at 21:00 UTC, so the second half of the horizon is a closed market.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding clock-hours have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable with null assessment fields; no past opinion is reconstructed from later information. The single available slot is 2026-08-21T01:00:00Z, taken from the finalised history entry generated at 01:34:51Z, which published tail 12%, stress 59%, confidence 83% and a mixed dominant mode. For context established from independent research rather than provider history, the Nasdaq-100 declined on each of 17, 18, 19 and 20 August, and the 20 August session closed about 95 points above its low, so retracements stayed available throughout the drawdown.
outlookSummary: The horizon runs from the current European pre-open through a full European and US session and then ends inside the weekend futures halt. Early European hours are scored at low tail risk on the contained, two-sided overnight band. Conditional risk rises into the US pre-market and peaks in the 13:00-14:00 UTC hour, which contains both the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI and is published as the narrow danger window. A second, slightly lower peak falls on the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close alongside weekend risk reduction with the Strait of Hormuz disruption unresolved. CME equity index futures halt at 21:00 UTC, so the final nine slots describe a deterministic closed-market state rather than a price-path forecast, and their scores step down accordingly. Every slot maps to EA_ON, because no persistent one-way structure is observed and the standing amplifiers, elevated long-end yields and the oil risk premium, are persistent conditions rather than fresh discontinuities. The Jackson Hole symposium runs 27-29 August, beyond this horizon and with no published speech times, so it is described here rather than listed as a timed event.
